quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.phenomenon: main theorem: 'Let G=GL_n or SL_n. Suppose (g,n)=(1,n) or (2,2). Then ... (1) the P=W conjecture; (2) the PI=WI conjecture; (3) the P=W conjecture for a symplectic resolution.' Line 305 adds that the P=W and PI=WI conjectures for M_Dol(PGL_n) hold too, citing 4.3.
quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.reader_note: items (1)/(2) are named without restating which cohomology theory they refer to (twisted 1.1, singular ordinary-cohomology 1.3, or intersection-cohomology 1.2). The proof at 308-316 routes through the SL_n versions of 1.2, 1.3 and 1.5. Recorded as a notation point; no repair attempted.

quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.phenomenon: twisted Betti/Dolbeault moduli require d coprime with n; footnote at 224: the untwisted Dolbeault space is recovered for d=0
quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.reader_note: the untwisted spaces used in Sections 6-8 are d=0, which is not coprime to n=2; the coprime hypothesis belongs to the twisted spaces only

quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.phenomenon: a PGL_n-Higgs bundle is an equivalence class of SL_n-Higgs bundles under tensorisation by an n-torsion line bundle
M_B is the affine GIT quotient of the relation-product set by G; it parametrizes semistable representations
Omega = Sing(Sigma) inside Sigma = Sing(M) inside M; Sigma is the quotient of Pic^0(C) x H^0(C,K_C) by the involution and has dimension 4; Omega is the branch locus with 16 points
quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.reader_note: the numbers 4 and 16 feeding the computations of 8.2/8.3 come from here

quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.phenomenon: q: M_iota -> M is 'quasi-etale of degree two, and branched along the singular locus Sigma of M_iota' (1523), while Sigma was defined as Sing(M) at 1124; the proof's last sentence says q is 'quasi-finite and branched along Sigma' (1533)
quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.reader_note: literal reading recorded; the branch locus is not reassigned here

quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.phenomenon: 6.30: 'The smooth locus M_Dol(X,SL_n)^sm is simply-connected for g>=2 and (g,n) not (2,2). In particular, pi_1(M^sm)=Z/2.' Here M = M_Dol(C,SL_2) is exactly the excluded case (g,n)=(2,2).
quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.reader_note: the 'in particular' clause concerns the excluded space and is obtained inside the proof (1772-1785) via the exact sequence; wording recorded, not adjusted

quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.phenomenon: the inverse images of Omega are the 16 points Omega_iota; the inverse images of Theta are the 32 points Theta_iota
quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.reader_note: 6.23 makes Omega_iota the singular locus of M_iota; the counts are recorded as written

quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.phenomenon: the action of Gamma on M lifts to M_iota and, with the deck transformation of q, yields a group of symmetries of order 32
R f_* QQ of M-tilde shifted by 6 is IC_M plus QQ_Sigma[4](-1) plus QQ_Omega(-3), and the same on the Betti side with Sigma_B, Omega_B; in cohomology H^{*-2}(Sigma)(-1) and H^{*-6}(Omega)(-3)
quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.reader_note: these shifts are absorbed into the P/W indices in 7.2 and 7.3

quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.phenomenon: IH^*(X,L) = H^{*-dim X}(X, IC_X(L)); compact support uses the Verdier dual of IC_X(L)
E(X) and IE(X) use (-1)^d on d-th compactly supported cohomology and Gr^W_{p+q} with Hodge bidegree (p,q)
after 8.3 the mixed Hodge structure on IH^d_c(M_B) is asserted to be of Hodge-Tate type by absence of cancellation
quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.reader_note: used downstream in 8.4 and 8.17; recorded as written

quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.phenomenon: H^*(Sigma) is isomorphic to H^*(S) with S the singular Kummer surface; the restriction to a general fibre is injective; hence H^d(Sigma) has top perversity d
M_Dol(A,SL_n) is K^{(n)}(A x C) and M_B(A,SL_n) is K^{(n)}(C^* x C^*); the P=W claim for the symplectic resolution is for K^[n](A x C)
quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.reader_note: A is an elliptic curve here; the appendix relabels an abelian surface as A (2355 footnote)

quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.phenomenon: in that section A denotes an abelian surface, not a curve of genus one as in the rest of the paper

9.1-9.10 (including 9.8) are not counted: line 339 states the degenerations are not strictly used in the proof of the main theorem.

shared_scope: The selected PI=WI target is M=M_Dol(C,SL2), C compact of genus2, untwisted degree0, rank2, trivial determinant and trace-free Higgs field, rational intersection cohomology. It is not an assertion for arbitrary genus/rank or ordinary cohomology of the singular space.
Keep P_k IH*(M)=Psi* W_{2k} IH*(M_B) and Gamma=Pic^0(C)[2] invariant/variant splitting, exact perverse shifts, chi-ample alpha, and distinction from ordinary cohomology of the symplectic resolution.

The quasi-etale cover M_iota and its smooth locus carry equivariant Higgs bundles with hyperelliptic involution, six Weierstrass points and trace(h_w)=0. Those auxiliary conditions are not added as restrictions on every point of the target M.

The projective bundle R is on M_iota^sm, its Gamma_iota-invariant class is identified with IH^4(M)^Gamma; do not claim a universal bundle on M itself or replace intersection cohomology by ordinary cohomology.

General complex reductive G and any compact Riemann surface belong to support Theorem3.8; its square commutes up to isotopy, with cohomological commutativity, and symplectic choice only for GLn/SLn, (g,n)=(1,n) or(2,2). GL/PGL/genus-one consequences are support, not separate new claims.
